subject: Demo follow-up and POC commitments — performance & acceptance
messages:
From: Elena Morrow <elena@strivetech.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-11T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Demo follow-up: performance & POC scope

Hi Logan —

Thanks again for the demo today, really helpful to see the end-to-end latency improvements and the KV caching behavior. The team at StriveTech is aligned on running a short POC focused on our retrieval-augmented QA flows. High-level asks from our side:

- We need clear acceptance criteria for performance (latency/throughput), cost, and result quality so we can sign off internally.
- A measurement plan so we can reproduce results on our dataset (we attached a small sample).
- Security and deployment checklist (service accounts, VPC/VPN notes) — we’ll need that for our compliance review.

We’ve attached a 500-row sample corpus (strivetech-samples.jsonl) and a short doc describing our query distribution. Proposed POC window: ~3 weeks, kickoff week of Apr 20.

Can you send a one-page checklist and proposed success metrics so I can circulate to the product team?

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morrow
Sr. Product Manager, StriveTech

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morrow <elena@strivetech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: performance & POC scope

Hi Elena —

Great to meet the StriveTech team. Appreciate the sample dataset; that helps a lot. Below is a concise POC scope and acceptance checklist we typically use — I tuned the numbers to what we saw in the demo and what you said about expected load. If anything should be tighter/looser, tell us and we can update.

POC length: 3 weeks (kickoff Apr 20 — readout May 8)
Goal: Demonstrate production-quality inference for RAG QA at scale on your corpus with measurable latency, throughput, cost, and quality metrics.

Acceptance criteria (proposed) — must be reproducible using your samples and our test harness:
- Latency: p95 end-to-end response time <= 300 ms for 512-token prompts under steady-state traffic (see measurement notes).
- Throughput: sustain 150 QPS with <= 10% tail degradation over 10-minute windows.
- Cost: average generation cost <= $0.0008 per token (model/quantization profile to be confirmed).
- Quality: top-1 answer accuracy >= 88% on your annotated QA sample; hallucination incidents < 2% (we'll define examples and agreement criteria).

Measurement & evaluation plan:
1) Week 0 (prep): access & infra — we need a service account for API access, dataset in S3 or shared Drive, and your security questionnaire answers.
2) Week 1 (baseline): run baseline runs against a small holdout set, collect latency traces and token-level cost.
3) Week 2 (optimizations): enable caching/kv-prefix, try quantized variant, measure throughput and p95 changes.
4) Week 3 (validation & readout): complete full-run, generate final report with cost breakdown, latency CDF, and quality assessment.

Ownership & roles:
- Redwood owner (technical): Logan Wright — POC lead, performance validation.
- Redwood ops: Ben Carter — will coordinate dedicated pool and load tests.
- Redwood ML engineer: Marissa Cole — evaluation scripts, metrics collection.
- StriveTech owner: Elena Morrow — data & success sign-off.

Required artifacts from StriveTech:
- Full sample dataset (we can work with S3 link or Drive).
- Annotated validation set for quality checks (at least 200 items).
- Security questionnaire + point of contact for network access.

Deliverables from Redwood:
- Weekly status notes, latency+throughput traces, cost per token breakdown, and a final POC report with recommendations (quantization, batching, routing).

Attachments: SLA-draft-v1.pdf (for commercial baseline)

Next steps:
- Elena: confirm kickoff week of Apr 20 and share dataset location.
- Logan/Ben/Marissa: prepare a short test harness and a load schedule; we’ll send a HubSpot activity and calendar invite.

I’ll start the internal ops runbook this week and post the test plan link once ready.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
--- Attachment: SLA-draft-v1.pdf (application/pdf, stub)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-13T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: performance & POC scope

Looping Marcus in for capacity planning. Quick ops notes and proposed owners:

- Ben: coordinate dedicated GPU pool for the 3-week window; estimate: 2 x A30 equiv for baseline, scale to 4 for load runs.
- Marcus: set up synthetic load harness (k6 + token-level instrumentation) and run an initial ramp to validate p95 numbers. Capture token emission timing and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Marissa: write evaluation script that computes top-1 accuracy, F1 for QA pairs, and a hallucination flag (we'll define heuristics). Also prepare the seed prompt templates.

Risks & mitigations:
- If p95 > 350ms at 150 QPS, we drop to model variant with lower latency (quantized 8-bit) — Marissa will own the trade-off table.
- Data access delays — ask StriveTech to provide S3 credentials or Drive link by Apr 16 to keep timeline.

Budget/Commercial note: If we need dedicated capacity beyond week 2 load runs, we should flag for a short-term reserved commit; I’ll put an estimate in the deal record (DEAL-4721).

Action items (by Apr 16):
- Marcus: first load-run + traces.
- Marissa: evaluation harness + initial metrics.
- Logan: send service account instructions to Elena and push HubSpot activity.

Ben
Head of POC Operations, Redwood Inference
